title: VoltPilot v2 Entity Config / Telemetry / Command Payloads
description: The E1a half of the v2 entity topic family (edge-desired-arbitration.md owns desired + arbitration): the per-entity retained CONFIG the Go core publishes on the local bus, the per-entity local TELEMETRY Layer 1 publishes, the core-owned retained COMMAND, and the cloud->edge entity-registry PUSH that transports the config set to the device. A brand-new contract, so schema_version starts at 1.0 (v2 README coexistence philosophy #4). The entity descriptor is the wire form of the cloud entity registry (measurement_point rows carrying entity_type/capabilities/guard config); capabilities follow the D-14 command vocabulary and guard limits + failsafe live HERE, in registry config, per decision D-9 - a failsafe carried only in a plan would die with the plan.

x-topics.registry-push: ems/{tenant_id}/{site_id}/{device_id}/v2/entities  (Cloud -> Edge, QoS1, RETAINED - one message carrying the device's full entity set; the proven inverter-config/sources-config pattern. An empty entities array removes every entity; an empty payload clears the retained slot outright (device unclaimed - the provisioning clearRetained precedent).)
x-topics.config: edge/entities/{entity_id}/config  (core -> Layer 1 / flows, RETAINED per entity - $defs/config. Publishing an empty payload clears the retained config = entity removed.)
x-topics.command: edge/entities/{entity_id}/command  (core -> Layer 1, RETAINED per entity - $defs/command. Published ONLY by the core after arbitration + guards; the successor of the retained edge/setpoint. An empty payload clears the retained command = nothing commanded.)

x-semantics.identity: The entity_id in every payload MUST equal the {entity_id} topic segment; consumers ignore mismatches (the v1 topic==payload identity rule).
x-semantics.failsafe: guards.failsafe.behavior is what the entity falls back to when nothing commands it (no active desired, stale plan - decision D-9): 'self-consumption' (storage: the v1 guards.SelfConsumption fallback), 'off' (consumers: safe state), 'release' (return the device to its native behavior, clear limits), 'measure-only' (entity is never actuated at all - grid meters, uncontrolled producers).
x-semantics.charge_from_grid_allowed: Storage guard posture per decision D-8: false OR ABSENT = the entity must never charge from the grid (commanded charge clamped to measured available PV; unknown PV blocks charge entirely). Only an explicit true releases the clamp.
x-semantics.signs: Shared with mqtt-telemetry-2.0 and the command vocabulary: storage setpoint_kw/battery_power_kw + = charge, - = discharge; grid power_kw + = import, - = export; generation is only ever capped (limit_kw/limit_pct reduce-only), never commanded to produce; consumer setpoint_kw + = consume (never negative - V2G out of scope).

entity_id.description: Entity id, MQTT-topic-safe (the provisioning ref pattern). The cloud entity registry row UUID is the recommended form.

entity_type.description: Domain type on top of the capability model (plan decision D10). OPEN vocabulary since E1b: the data-driven platform type CATALOG (services/api entitytypes/catalog.json) is the truth for known types - adding a type is catalog data + an optional driver, never a schema release. Catalog types today: battery-hybrid, producer, grid-meter, wallbox, heating-rod, generic-load. Consumers key BEHAVIOR on the declared capabilities and guards, never on the type string alone: no actuate list (or a measure-only failsafe) = measure-only; storage-shaped guard limits = the storage guard chain incl. D-8; max_generation_kw = producer reduce-only caps; otherwise the consumer clamp ([0, max_consumption_kw], + = consume).

channels.description: Flat numeric readings keyed by channel name (snake_case). Values are always numbers; a boolean state is 0/1.

capabilities.description: What the entity can report (measure) and what it may be commanded (actuate). The actuate command names are the D-14 vocabulary shared with edge-desired and mqtt-schedule-2.0. A measure-only entity (grid meter) simply has no actuate list.

min.description: Lower bound for numeric commands (e.g. setpoint_kw: -max_discharge).

guard_limits.description: Per-entity guard chain inputs (decision D-9: limits live in registry config, not in plans; the generalization of the v1 env-derived guards.Limits). All optional - an absent limit skips that clamp, EXCEPT charge_from_grid_allowed where absent = NOT allowed (D-8).

charge_from_grid_allowed.description: D-8: absent = NOT allowed; only explicit true releases the solar-only-charge clamp.

max_generation_kw.description: Producer nameplate cap: a limit_kw command is additionally clamped to [0, max_generation_kw]; limits only ever reduce.

max_consumption_kw.description: Consumer rated cap (E1b, additive): setpoint_kw and limit_kw on a consumer entity are additionally clamped to [0, max_consumption_kw]. Consumers are only ever commanded to CONSUME (+ = consume, per the D-14 sign convention); a negative consumer setpoint is clamped to 0 - feeding in from a consumer (V2G) is out of scope.

min_on_seconds.description: Consumer cycle guard (Verbrauchssteuerung Inkrement 3, additive): once commanded ON the entity is held ON for at least this long before a commanded switch-off takes effect - a TEMPORAL device-protection invariant enforced by the edge's stateful cycle guard (restrict-only: it delays/holds, never raises beyond a previously granted level). Absent = axis inactive (no invented protection).

min_off_seconds.description: Consumer cycle guard (additive): after a commanded switch-off the entity stays OFF for at least this long; a wish to switch ON earlier is held with an honest reason ('wartet - Mindestpause'). Absent = axis inactive.

max_starts_per_day.description: Consumer cycle guard (additive): at most this many commanded starts per site-local day; further starts are held until the day rolls over. Absent = axis inactive.

ramp_kw_per_min.description: Consumer cycle guard (additive): the commanded setpoint may change by at most this many kW per minute while ON (both directions - a hold toward the wish, never a raise beyond it). Absent = axis inactive.

descriptor.description: One entity as the registry knows it. driver is an OPTIONAL opaque connection block for Layer-1 self-wiring (brand/model/family/communication/connection in the v1 sources busEntry shape); E1a carries it through verbatim, the v2 driver layer consumes it in a later increment.

edge_source_id.description: The edge-local source id this entity was adopted from (:8484 sources selection; the cloud pin measurement_point.edge_source_id). OPTIONAL + ADDITIVE (2026-07-29, vp-vier-erzeuger-p9 PR 4a): lets the device map its OWN source readings onto the entity for its LOCAL display - deterministic instead of order-guessing. An old edge ignores it.

config.title: edge/entities/{entity_id}/config payload
config.description: The retained per-entity config: the registry descriptor plus schema_version and the registry revision it came from.

edge_source_id.description: The adoption pin, mirrored from the registry descriptor (D-17) - the config IS the descriptor plus the applied revision.

revision.description: The registry push revision this config was applied from (echoed in the status heartbeat).

ts.description: Observation time (RFC 3339, UTC); absent = receive time.

command.title: edge/entities/{entity_id}/command payload
command.description: The guard-clamped command state the driver layer executes - core-owned, retained, re-derived continuously (the edge/setpoint successor). commands carries the granted values keyed by the D-14 vocabulary; an absent limit_kw/limit_pct means NO limit and MUST clear any previously applied limit (the 1.0 pv_limit_kw clearing rule).

control_enabled.description: The v1 two-gate posture carried per entity: false = the driver layer must not write (readbacks still run so the UI shows actual state).

source.description: Who the granted command came from - documented values: 'plan' (market desire from the plan executor), 'desired' (arbitration winner), 'failsafe' (registry failsafe active). Open set.

registry_push.title: ems/{t}/{s}/{d}/v2/entities payload (entity-registry push)
registry_push.description: The cloud entity registry pushed to the device, retained: the device's FULL entity set in one message (subscribe = converge, reconnect = re-converge; the retained-config pattern proven three times over, D-11 rationale). The edge diffs against its persisted set: new/changed entities are (re)published as per-entity retained configs, removed entities get their retained config + command cleared.

revision.description: Opaque registry revision (the api uses the push's published_at instant). The edge echoes the applied revision in its status heartbeat 'entities' block, so the cloud can verify convergence.

entities.description: May be empty: the device has no v2 entities (all local per-entity configs are cleared).
